qti-assessment-test.title: Feeling Good Institute - TEAM-CBT Assessment Resistance & Deliberate Practice Empathy Skills (APA / ASWB CE Demo)

qti-assessment-item.title: Apply the TEAM-CBT Disarming Technique when a client criticizes therapy homework or clinician empathy.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Apply the TEAM-CBT Disarming Technique when a client criticizes therapy homework or clinician empathy.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: At the start of Session 3, an anxious client says: 'Those mood logs were a complete waste of my week, and honestly it feels like you are just reading from a checklist instead of listening to me.' Which therapist response accurately executes the TEAM-CBT Disarming Technique?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: 'You are making a really important point - the mood logs felt tedious this week, and when I jumped to forms too fast it left you feeling unheard rather than supported. Tell me more about what felt most off so I can really get it right.'
'Let's examine that statement together on a Daily Mood Log, because 'complete waste' sounds like all-or-nothing thinking and mind-reading.'
'I hear that you are frustrated, though randomized trials show written homework doubles CBT recovery rates when clients stick with it.'
'Perhaps cognitive behavioral therapy is not the right modality for you right now, so let's pause all structured tools indefinitely.'

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Effective disarming validates the genuine grain of truth in the client's criticism without defensiveness and pairs thought/feeling empathy with gentle inquiry.
Incorrect. Labeling cognitive distortions during an alliance rupture violates TEAM order (Empathy before Methods) and intensifies defensiveness.
Incorrect. Adding 'though/but' to cite research invalidates the client's lived experience and turns empathy into persuasion.
Incorrect. Passive withdrawal abandons the collaborative TEAM framework instead of repairing the alliance through accurate empathy.

qti-assessment-item.title: Execute Paradoxical Agenda Setting to melt outcome resistance in chronic depression or anxiety.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Execute Paradoxical Agenda Setting to melt outcome resistance in chronic depression or anxiety.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: During Agenda Setting with a perfectionistic professional seeking relief from generalized worry, the client repeatedly responds with 'yes, but if I stop worrying I will miss a critical deadline.' What is the core clinical move in TEAM-CBT Assessment of Resistance?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Honor the protective advantages of the client's worry (conscientiousness, vigilance, high standards) and invite the client to argue for why lowering worry might still be worthwhile before attempting any anxiety-reduction method.
Immediately assign a 60-minute interoceptive exposure hierarchy to extinguish somatic anxiety symptoms before resistance hardens.
Prove to the client with workplace performance statistics that chronic worry impairs executive function and causes missed deadlines.
Skip Brief Mood Survey tracking whenever resistance appears so pre- and post-session symptom scores do not discourage the client.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Positive reframing and sitting with open hands shift the clinician out of persuasion so the client articulates intrinsic motivation to reduce excess worry.
Incorrect. Launching exposure methods before resolving outcome and process resistance produces homework non-adherence and premature dropout.
Incorrect. Debating the client triggers psychological reactance ('salesman vs. reluctant buyer') and reinforces their defense of worrying.
Incorrect. Routine session-by-session Testing (the 'T' in TEAM) remains foundational for detecting alliance dips and symptom change.

qti-assessment-item.title: Interpret Brief Mood Survey (Testing) discrepancies between symptom reduction and therapeutic alliance scores.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Interpret Brief Mood Survey (Testing) discrepancies between symptom reduction and therapeutic alliance scores.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Post-session Testing reveals a client's depression score dropped from 14 to 8, yet their Helpful/Empathy rating for the session fell to 12 out of 20. According to TEAM-CBT measurement-based care guidelines, what should the clinician prioritize first?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Warmly thank the client for their honesty on the Empathy scale, explore what felt missed or rushed in the session using disarming and thought/feeling empathy, and repair the rupture before celebrating symptom drops.
Proceed directly to relapse-prevention planning since a 6-point depression reduction confirms the cognitive method worked.
Average the depression and empathy subscores into a composite index and intervene only if both metrics worsen simultaneously.
Explain that tough cognitive interventions naturally lower warmth scores when therapists challenge core beliefs.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Any Empathy score below near-perfect (20/20) signals an alliance rupture that predicts future relapse or dropout unless openly explored with curiosity and disarming.
Incorrect. Unaddressed alliance ruptures undermine sustained recovery even when single-session symptom scores briefly improve.
Incorrect. Symptom severity and therapeutic alliance measure distinct clinical constructs and must never be collapsed into a single blended score.
Incorrect. Explaining away low alliance ratings blames the client rather than taking responsibility for empathetic attunement.
